the acute phase of stroke is associated with the development of intravascular coagulation and the depression of fibrinolytic activity, which leads to the development of red blood cell rouleaux and aggregates.
the acute ischemic stroke leads to the changes in homeostasis and T-lymphocyte immunity, which are more expressed in patients with poor clinical outcome.

the acute period of stroke is characterized by the activation of the blood coagulation, the inhibition of fibrinolitic activity, the increase in the number of "rough" erythrocytes, their aggregation and the decrease in the level of T-cell immunity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of homeostasis, rheological and immune properties of blood in the acute phase of ischemic stroke, and the correlation between these parameters and the clinical course of the disease.
the changes in homeostasis and the state of immunity in acute period of ischemia stroke.
the changes of hemostasis and immune system in acute stroke and the relationship of these changes with stroke outcome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study provides evidence that the immune response to the stroke may play a significant role in the development of the disease.
stroke patients with poor outcome have more severe and long-term changes in homeostasis and immune system.
the immune system is not only an integral component of the pathophysiology of stroke but it is also a potential therapeutic target.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the acute ischemic stroke is a multifactorial disease with a number of different mechanisms.
in the acute period after ischemic stroke the intravascular coagulation and fibrinolysis depression happen, and the changes of red blood cells are observed.
in ischemic stroke there are changes in the homeostasis, rheological properties of blood and T-lymphocyte immunity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system plays a crucial role in the pathogenesis of ischemic stroke.
we have to pay more attention to the role of blood cells in the development of ischemic stroke and to find the best way to treat it.
